The SSH driver gets the pending_cleanup teardown retry the stock cleanup sweep calls (stock SSH has none, so an SSH lease moved to pending_cleanup by an Interrupt or the orphaned-active-lease sweep failed with destroy_failed forever). It returns a stopped receipt only when the legacy run provably never launched an adapter or Crew's stop command on the host finds no process of the run left; otherwise it throws and the sweep retries with its backoff, with a crew.remote_stop activity per attempt and one crew.remote_stop.escalated activity when the attempts reach the stock cap.

A Claude result with subtype success and is_error false is never classified as claude_auth_required, and the login-prompt markers (unauthorized, please run /login, ...) are matched only against Claude's own output: the parsed result and errors, stderr, plain-text stdout lines, and assistant events the CLI flags with an error. Stock matched them against every stdout line, so a successful run whose tool output printed an OpenAPI "401 Unauthorized" and that exited 255 after its final result (a background process stopped by the terminal-result cleanup) was labelled claude_auth_required, which showed the auth-repair card, blocked the retry and switched the runtime. The run still ends failed (stock unmanaged background task policy); only the auth label is dropped.

Only the board (including the Cloud envelope actor, which is a board actor) may apply an onboarding seed; an agent could otherwise create a ceo agent, a goal, a project and a root task. assertBoard is added to the existing authz import.

Agents in Crew companies cannot create, update, archive or delete projects or project workspaces (403 crew_board_only); the MCP create_project tool calls the same REST route with the agent token, so it is refused too. Workspace runtime controls stay stock.
Agents in Crew companies cannot hard-delete issues, even their own (403 crew_board_only); the delete path bypasses the issue write hook.

An agent in a Crew company checks out only issues that are unassigned or already assigned to itself (409 crew_checkout_forbidden): it cannot take an issue assigned to another agent or waiting on a user such as the owner. Board checkout on behalf of an agent stays stock.

Agents in Crew companies cannot update execution workspaces (403 crew_board_only). Board only, because core has no per-agent workspace owner (runtime:manage is company-wide) and Crew agents run in place from their environment.

Deliver plugin events to the worker as a call (deliverEventAsCall, same 15-minute ceiling) instead of a notification, so the event's invocation scope is cleared when the handlers settle; a lingering scope made every unscoped worker-to-host call fail with INVOCATION_SCOPE_DENIED for 15 minutes after each event. Other notifications are unchanged. Upstream text: plans/261010-0020-crew-v3-r3/reports/upstream-plugin-event-scope.md in the Crew repo.

Mount the Crew contribution router (/api/crew/companies/:companyId/...) right after the approval routes, behind the board mutation guard. A Crew contributor (a core viewer flagged in the Crew plugin table crew_contributors) files issues and comments into the Crew plugin table crew_contributions, never into core tables, so agents cannot read pending or rejected content; the company owner approves by posting through the stock board routes with an idempotency key, and the router finds the created core record itself. The server writes crew_contributions and crew_contributors, the second set of plugin tables it writes after crew_runtime_waits. Browser-session board actors with a user id only (agents, board API keys and the local implicit board get 403, because board keys live on the machines that run agents); request bodies are moved off req.body before any check so HTTP logs and error reports never carry pending content; roles are read from the database, not via assertCompanyAccess; no activity log, live event or plugin event is emitted. The same router mounts the Crew project-access routes (/api/crew/companies/:companyId/project-access, plugin table crew_project_access): the owner chooses which projects each non-owner member sees in the Crew UI, contributions to a project the author cannot see are rejected on create and approve, and core API reads are unchanged. Because it is mounted before the stock plugin routes, the same router also holds /api/plugins/... requests that arrive while the startup plugin load (app.locals.bundledPluginsStartup) is still running, at most 10 seconds, so requests in the first seconds after a restart reach a registered plugin worker instead of getting 502 No worker registered or 503 Plugin worker is not running; after the load settles, or when it takes longer, requests pass straight through to the stock routes. The same router also mounts the Crew Jev routes (/api/crew/companies/:companyId/jev, plugin tables crew_jev_settings, crew_jev_machines, crew_jev_gate_events and crew_jev_shadow, which the server writes): owner-only settings, OpenRouter key (stored as the company secret crew-jev-openrouter and never returned), stats, gate events and shadow comparisons under the same browser-session owner rule and body removal, plus /jev/machine/pull and /jev/machine/events, which accept only requests HMAC-signed with the machine key under the same rules as the Crew plugin machine webhook.

entries.description: A board viewer of a Crew company may read an allowlisted set of crew.core plugin data keys (POST /plugins/crew.core/data/:key, the keys the Crew UI reads on pages a viewer can open) for that company; the stock bridge scope treats the POST as a write and returns 403 Viewer access is read-only, which leaves the Crew UI unusable for viewers. Only the crew.core data route is widened, only for allowlisted keys (a new plugin data key stays closed to viewers until it is added), only when the company is in a readable Crew config (a broken config fails closed) and an active user membership with role viewer is confirmed from the database; every other plugin, company, actor and route (bridge/data, bridge/action, actions/:key, scoped API routes) keeps the stock check, and every other viewer write stays 403.

Expose the stock acknowledgeRemoteStop on the heartbeat service. Stock acknowledges a Stop right after the lease release, but the SSH stop and its termination receipt land later in the background (H3), so a legacy SSH run stayed at executionCancellation.state = requested and later user messages were held; Crew calls it again once the receipt is written, before resumeRemoteStopComments, as the stock cleanup sweep does after a provider receipt.

Run Crew's replay of stranded skipped wakes on every scheduler tick, after the stock periodic recovery. A stage handoff cancels the executor's run and wakes the next participant while the run's lease is still held, so stock skips the wake (execution_reconciliation_required) and never retries it. Crew replays it from the SSH lease release hook (H3), but when the lease is older than the reaper's staleness the reaper tick moves it to pending_cleanup and releases it through the SSH cleanup retry (P8) before executeRun unwinds, so H3 never runs and the review stage stalls (stock review recovery only retries a participant whose own run ended). The tick replays such a wake once, when its hold is gone and the agent got no wake or run on the issue since.

A run that reassigns its own issue (executor to reviewer, reviewer to integrator) is no longer cancelled with issue_reassigned. Stock killed the requesting run before the provider printed its final result, so the run ended cancelled without usage or cost. The run now ends on its own and records usage like any run; the new assignee's wake re-adopts the still-running run as the issue's execution holder, is deferred behind it, and is promoted when it releases, so the two never run the issue side by side. A board user or another agent reassigning still cancels the previous assignee's run as stock does.

Queue the missing_issue_comment retry only when the run's agent is still the issue's assignee. Since a run that reassigns its own issue is no longer cancelled (C11), a run that handed off without posting a comment ended succeeded and stock queued a status-only comment wake for the previous assignee; that wake took the issue execution lock (then was cancelled as issue_assignee_changed) while the new assignee's deferred wake kept waiting. The run's comment status is now not_applicable with a lifecycle event, and the new assignee starts as soon as the run releases the issue.

A legacy run that leaves its issue in_progress after splitting the work into child issues gets no issue_disposition_repair wake while an open child has a live execution path (a queued or running run, or a queued or deferred wake), in every workspace mode. Stock counted children only for a shared workspace and only in the same project workspace, so the Crew assistant was woken again right after creating its children (one extra paid run) just to write that the root waits on them. A child that only waits (on a human owner, or on this agent's review) does not count, so the parent is still asked to act on it.

entries.anchor: logger.error({ err, runId: run.id }, "failed to promote another agent's deferred wake after cleanup");
entries.description: After an unsuccessful legacy run has released its environment lease, promote a wake another agent (a review participant or a new assignee) deferred behind it on the same issue, through the stock release admission. A conversation run that ends failed, timed_out or interrupted releases the issue while it still owns its environment lease, so the stock release sees execution_owner_active for the run itself and only plans recovery (recoveryOnly) without draining the deferred queue. Stock then retried after cleanup only the run's own agent's deferred wake, so a reviewer's execution_review_requested wake, deferred when the executor moved its own issue to in_review (C11) and the SSH session dropped at the end (exit 255, adapter_failed), stayed deferred until someone commented (TPS-246). The retry goes through the same release admission, so recovery holds, an acknowledged Stop, unconfirmed remote cleanup and a still-held lease keep the wake deferred as before.
